clue.text: Anglican character has idiot getting in stew

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the fool is placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church
an ass is a fool
a character played by an actor is a role

explanation.surface: A churchgoing figure is in a stew because some idiot has barged in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anglican character' reads as one phrase describing a person, but the two words do separate jobs: the church abbreviation, and an actor's part.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a slow-cooked dish of meat and vegetables, which is a stew.

clue.text: Hear of snag in contract

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make out what someone said, as in 'I didn't quite get that'
third meaning: to pick up an illness

explanation.surface: Someone hears about a snag buried in a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: This is in fact a triple definition, with 'of' and 'in' as links. The surface invites 'snag in contract' as one idea, which it also happens to describe.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb can mean to make out a sound or to come down with a cold, and as a noun it means a hidden drawback.

clue.text: Sell now after adjustment indicating effect of inflation?

definitions.note: an adjective describing something that has been inflated

indicators.note: an adjustment changes things around, so the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Financial advice: sell your holdings now, after a price adjustment caused by inflation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' reads as rising prices; the definition means physical puffing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something swollen has been puffed up, so the word describes what inflating does to a balloon or a tyre.

clue.text: All sides except West admit defeat, mostly settled

indicators.note: except means leaving one compass point out of the full set

parts.note: the four compass points, East, North, South and West

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of the phrase, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to concede is to admit you have lost

explanation.surface: A team on every side, bar the west, concedes and settles.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points come in any order, so E, N and S are arranged to suit the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ensconced is to be comfortably established in a place, that is, settled in.

clue.text: Tip exceeding funds available?

parts.note: over means more than
your balance is the money left in your account

explanation.surface: A gratuity bigger than the money in your account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity, but it is the verb meaning to fall over; the rest reads as going beyond your balance.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbalance is to lose your equilibrium and topple, much as a vase tips.

clue.text: Go out live: revolutionary start for broadcast

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word for live is read backwards

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of broadcast

explanation.surface: A revolutionary goes out live at the start of a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out live' sounds like a TV transmission; the definition is the tide going out.
explanation.definitionFit: When the tide ebbs it flows away from the shore, so it goes out.

clue.text: Glue ear's picked up and measured

indicators.note: what the ear picks up is a sound, so the word for glue is taken by how it is said

parts.note: paste is a kind of glue

explanation.surface: A doctor's note: a case of glue ear has been detected and measured.
explanation.walkthrough: Glue ear is a real condition of fluid in the middle ear, which makes the surface plausible; here 'Glue' and 'ear' split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To pace a distance is to measure it out by counting steps.

clue.text: Second of spoons incorrect — not with fork

indicators.note: the second of a word is the letter in position two

parts.note: the second letter of spoons

indicators.note: not with means the abbreviation for with must be dropped

parts.note: incorrect means wrong
W is a standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Cutlery etiquette: the second spoon is wrong if not with a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is one tine of a fork, and the word also names a forked implement.

clue.text: Tea ready — and one gets bread

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
pat means ready or glib, as in an answer off pat
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Tea is ready, and each person gets some bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened flatbread from South Asia.

clue.text: Hurry after some food: a habit in Arab world

indicators.note: after places the hurrying word second, following the food word that is written later in the clue

parts.note: a dish is an item of food
to dash is to hurry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rushing about after a meal is a habit in Arab countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' reads as a custom, but it means a garment, as in a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishdasha is the long robe worn by men in the Arabian Gulf, a garment like a habit.

clue.text: Beefeater, market trader or squealer heading home?

definitions.text: Beefeater, market trader or squealer heading home?

parts.words: Beefeater, market trader or squealer heading home?
parts.note: surface reading: a list of people, a Tower of London guard, a stallholder and an informer running off

parts.words: Beefeater, market trader or squealer heading home?
parts.note: setter's reading: the piggies of the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy', each played on a child's toe

explanation.surface: An odd line-up: a Tower guard, a stallholder, or an informer heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme one piggy goes to market, one has roast beef, and one cries 'wee wee wee' all the way home; each piggy is a toe being counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is a childish word for a toe, and toes are the piggies of the nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Fish around island proving source of energy

indicators.note: around means the fish wraps about the island

parts.note: a bass is a fish
IOM is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Fish swimming around an island turn out to be a source of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Biomass is plant or animal matter burnt or processed as fuel, a renewable energy source.

clue.text: Greeting that boy will love

parts.note: he'll is short for he will, that boy being he
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: That boy will love the greeting he gets.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the commonest word said when meeting someone, a salutation.

clue.text: Dear — a thousand for instrument that's not the largest

parts.note: baby is an endearment, like dear
a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Pricey: a thousand paid for an instrument that isn't even the biggest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like expensive, which fits a price, but it is a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby grand is the smallest kind of grand piano, smaller than a concert grand.

clue.text: Peach with skins served up, and rest of refreshment?

parts.note: a peach is a beauty, something excellent

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: fruit skins are peels

explanation.surface: A peach served with its skin on, followed by the rest of a refreshing snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' looks like the remainder, but it means sleep; 'refreshment' means restoring your looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauty sleep is extra rest thought to refresh the appearance, so it is restorative rest.

clue.text: Lumière's partner and child

definitions.meaning: first meaning: French for sound, as in ... et lumière, a sound and light show

explanation.surface: The Lumière brothers' film partner and his child.
explanation.walkthrough: Lumière suggests the French cinema pioneers; it is the light in son et lumière, an outdoor show of sound and light at a historic building.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for sound, which pairs with light in that show title, and in English it means a male offspring.

clue.text: One hitting on record producer who's driving force behind Kids in America?

definitions.text: driving force behind Kids in America

indicators.note: something on record is heard when played, so the word for one hitting is taken by its sound

parts.note: someone who socks, or punches
a mother produces children; the American spelling is required

explanation.surface: A boxer's record producer behind the 1981 hit 'Kids in America'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kids in America' is a Kim Wilde song, but here it means American children, whom this mother drives to games and practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer mom is an American suburban mother who ferries her children to sports and activities.

clue.text: Way of getting fit name, a nicest variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so these letters come in another arrangement

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
the fodder, rearranged

explanation.surface: Choosing the nicest variety of fitness regime by its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Callanetics is a trademarked exercise system of small repeated movements, a fitness method.

clue.text: Labour's conclusion — government must call an election now

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pregnancy carried to full term concludes with labour

definitions.text: government must call an election now
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the point when a parliament's fixed period expires

explanation.surface: Labour has reached its finish, and the government must go to the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour suggests the British political party, which suits the election; the first meaning is about childbirth, which arrives when a pregnancy reaches its full term.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnancy's term ends in labour, and a parliamentary term ends with an election being called.

clue.text: Arranged diamonds in elaborate decoration

indicators.note: in means the card suit goes inside the following word
something elaborate is worked over intricately, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: Diamonds set into an ornate decoration, carefully arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Coordinated things have been organised to work together, so they are arranged.

clue.text: No cigar processed without chemicals

indicators.note: processed material is broken down and reworked, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: No processed cigars: they're grown without chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts processed and natural tobacco; 'processed' is really the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is farmed without artificial fertilisers or pesticides, that is, chemical-free.

clue.text: Singular dad's resort

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
pa is a word for father

explanation.surface: An odd father's holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like odd or unusual, but it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a resort town built around mineral springs.

clue.text: Beer belly after working out?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: six cans of beer sold together
second meaning: well-defined stomach muscles from exercise

explanation.surface: A beer belly, after working out what caused it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beer belly' runs together as one phrase in the surface, but the clue splits after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a pack of six beer cans and toned abdominal muscles, an ironic pair.

clue.text: Creates spaces to accommodate sexual identity

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the identity sits inside the spaces

parts.note: an en is a printer's space half the width of an em
gender is a sexual identity

explanation.surface: A designer builds spaces that accommodate every sexual identity.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, an en is a unit of space, so ens are spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender is to bring about or cause, so engenders means creates.

clue.text: Released by wingers, Arsenal shot comes close

indicators.note: the wingers are the outside players, so the word lets go of its two end letters
shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the football club with its outer letters gone

explanation.surface: An Arsenal shot set up by the wingers comes close to scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; the surface is a match report.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that nears another thing comes close to it.

clue.text: Backing for official nabbing team's dodgy dealer?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole is read from the end
nabbing means catching hold, so the official holds the team inside

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official
a team of eleven, as in football or cricket

explanation.surface: Support for a referee caught taking the team's money: a dodgy dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixer arranges things by underhand means, a shady operator who rigs deals.

clue.text: Easy with this to make movie stars' demands?

definitions.text: Easy with this to make movie
definitions.meaning: first meaning: added to Easy it gives the 1969 film Easy ...
second meaning: the list of extras a performer requires in a contract

explanation.surface: How easy it is for film stars to make demands.
explanation.walkthrough: A rider is a clause added to a contract, famously listing a celebrity's backstage requirements.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity riders spell out a star's requirements, and Easy Rider is a classic road movie.

clue.text: Charge bloke and partner in restaurant?

parts.note: a bloke is a man
a date is someone you take out to dinner

explanation.surface: A restaurant bill: what to charge a man and his dinner companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a restaurant bill, but it means an official instruction or duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an authoritative commission, a task someone is charged with.

clue.text: Slip into Ferrari every so often

indicators.note: every so often means taking only some letters at regular gaps

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters; that they also sit together inside the name is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A slide into a Ferrari now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so it means to slip up.

clue.text: Gem pedlar emerging from behind pockets

indicators.note: read from behind means read from the back end towards the front
the phrase pockets the answer, holding it inside its letters

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A pedlar coming out from behind pockets a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious stone, a variety of beryl.

clue.text: Discharge a lot leaving hospital with you and me

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the hospital abbreviation goes

parts.note: much means a lot
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
us is you and me together

explanation.surface: A big discharge from hospital for the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' and 'hospital' suggest a patient being sent home; the definition is bodily fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucus is the slimy fluid secreted by membranes, such as nasal discharge.

clue.text: Creator of lines, dissolute chap penning bad poem meets resistance

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the poem's letters are reworked
penning means enclosing, so the chap holds the rest inside him

parts.note: a rake is a debauched man
the fodder, rearranged
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A debauched poet writes a bad poem and gets a hostile reception.
